case_name: Rajat Gandhi v. State Of Punjab And Another

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Rajat Gandhi, husband; Manju Gandhi and another, parents-in-law; Aarti Sareen, married sister-in-law

facts_of_case: The petitioners seek quashing of FIR No.253 dated 1.7.2009 registered at Police Station Civil Lines, Amritsar City for the offences under Sections 406 and 498-A Indian Penal Code and all subsequent proceedings arising therefrom on the basis of compromise.

legal_principles.principle: Matrimonial disputes can be amicably settled, and the court may quash proceedings in such cases.
legal_principles.held: Keeping in view the matrimonial dispute having been amicably settled, it would be just and expedient to terminate the proceedings by quashing the FIR.
cited_cases: B.S. Joshi and others v. State of Haryana (Year) X SCC Y

legal_principles.principle: The court may consider the compromise reached between parties in deciding whether to quash proceedings.
legal_principles.held: In terms of the settlement reached at, it has inter alia been resolved that Rajat Gandhi would handover a draft of `7,80,000/- to the complainant Ruchika Gandhi in Court when her statement in the case for divorce by mutual consent is recorded by the Court concerned.

outcome.final_order: The settlement reached at has been placed on record as Annexure P5 in Crl. Misc. No. M-16497 of 2010.

use_for_drafting: quashing FIRs in domestic violence cases
